material.name: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy
material.initial_state: inert gas atomised feedstock with spherical powder

intervention.description: Processing of inert gas atomised feedstock to produce dense bulk material

structure.description: Dense bulk material with microstructure comprising two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases and an additional phase with a complex crystal structure precipitating during SPS processing
phases: two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases
additional phase with a complex crystal structure
microstructure: no coarsening of microstructural features occurs

evidence_units.mechanism: High cooling rate in atomisation results in spherical powder; additional phase precipitation occurs during SPS without microstructural coarsening
evidence_spans: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of inert gas atomised feedstock enables the production of dense bulk material.
The high cooling rate in the atomisation process results in spherical powder with a microstructure comprising two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases.
An additional phase with a complex crystal structure precipitates during SPS processing, while no coarsening of microstructural features occurs.
SPS processing is suitable for the production of HEA bulk material.

intervention.description: Fabrication of cylindrical samples using graphite die and foil with thermal insulation

parameters.environment: argon flushed and evacuated (< 1 mbar) twice

structure.description: Cylindrical samples with diameter 40 mm and height 6 mm

evidence_units.mechanism: sintering at 1050 °C under vacuum conditions followed by passive cooling

outcome.measurement_method: calculated from passive cooling by water-cooled stamps

evidence_spans: The fabrication of cylindrical samples with a diameter of 40 mm and a height of 6 mm by spark plasma sintering (SPS) was conducted in a SPS KCE FCT-HP D 25-SI (FCT Systeme GmbH, Frankenblick, Germany), equipped with a pyrometer for temperature measurement.
Therefore, a graphite die and graphite foil with a thickness of 0.3 mm, placed between powder and punches as a release agent, were used.
In order to ensure uniform temperature distribution, the whole graphite tool was thermally insulated.
Prior to the sintering process, the recipient was flushed with argon and evacuated (< 1 mbar) twice.
After reaching a compaction pressure of 50 MPa, the samples were sintered at a temperature of 1050 °C for 10 min.
Subsequently, the samples were cooled passively and unregulated by the water-cooled stamps.
This results in a cooling rate of 150 K/min until 300 °C.

material.name: SPS-sintered AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 alloy
material.initial_state: sintered at 1050 °C for 10 min and cooled passively

intervention.description: Wear testing on cross-sections using a SRV-Tribometer

evidence_units.mechanism: reciprocating sliding against Al2O3 counter body at varying temperatures
evidence_spans: The investigation of reciprocating wear behaviour was carried out with an SRV-Tribometer (Optimol Instruments Prüftechnik GmbH, Munich, Germany) under atmospherical conditions.
Prior to wear investigations, the temperature was held constant for 5 min.
The applied parameters are summarised in Table 1 .
Force	26 N
Frequency	40 Hz
Time	900 s
Amplitude	0.5 mm
Counter Body	Al 2 O 3
Diameter	10 mm
Temperature	22 °C; 500 °C; 650 °C; 800 °C; 900°C
For the investigation of the resulting wear depth, a laser scanning microscope (LSM) Keyence VK-X200 (Keyence, Osaka, Japan) was used.
Furthermore, the wear tracks were analysed by SEM.
To determine the formed oxides within the wear tracks, XRD measurements were conducted after the wear investigations with point focus and a 0.5 mm collimator.

material.name: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5
material.composition: Atomised powder with measured composition: Al 20.1, Co 17.5, Cr 18.0, Fe 17.9, Ni 17.5, Ti 9.0 at.%; SPS sample with measured composition: Al 21.0, Co 17.3, Cr 17.7, Fe 17.5, Ni 17.5, Ti 8.9 at.%
material.initial_state: atomised powder with spherical particles, dendritic structure, fine phase distribution

intervention.description: Production of dense samples from atomised powder

structure.description: dense structure without porosity, multiphase microstructure with two bcc phases (B2 ordered and A2 disordered) and minor fcc phase

evidence_units.mechanism: Formation of additional tetragonal σ-phase and preservation of fine phase distribution due to fast cooling during atomisation and SPS processing suppresses decomposition but allows σ-phase formation.
evidence_spans: The resulting diffractograms of the XRD phase analyses for the feedstock and SPS samples are displayed in Figure 3 .
In accordance with the feedstock, the SPS samples exhibit a multiphase microstructure. However, additional phases appear after SPS processing.
For the SPS sample, an overall hardness of 750 ± 17 HV0.5 was measured.
In comparison to the same alloy produced by arc-melting, a distinct increase in the hardness occurs due to the formation of the additional σ-phase and a microstructure with a finer phase distribution

material.name: AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5
material.composition: SPS sample (see previous unit for composition)

intervention.description: Wear testing at temperatures from room temperature to 900 °C

structure.description: Surface covered with oxides; stable oxide film formation at high temperatures
microstructure: almost fully oxide-covered surface at 800 °C and 900 °C
smooth surface with grooves at 800 °C and 900 °C

evidence_units.mechanism: Formation of a stable, thick oxide film via tribo-oxidation protects the underlying metallic material, leading to increased wear resistance at elevated temperatures.
evidence_spans: With an increase in temperature from room temperature to 500 °C, a slight increase in the wear depth occurs, indicating a reduced wear resistance.
A further increase in test temperature results in a slight decrease in the wear depth.
For the wear investigations at 800 °C, a distinct reduction in wear depth occurs.
The highest wear resistance was proven for the test conducted at the highest temperature of 900 °C.
The decrease in wear depth proves the protection of the underlying material by tribo-oxidation and the formaton of a stable oxide film.
The additional maxima can be assigned to a spinel (structure type MgAl 2 O 4 ).

structure.description: Almost fully oxide-covered surface with some grooves

evidence_units.mechanism: Stable oxide film formation reduces friction and wear, with abrasive wear of oxides occurring on the surface.

comparison.baseline_state: tested at lower temperatures up to 800 °C

evidence_spans: The lowest COF was measured for the highest test temperature of 900 °C, with an average value of 0.85.
For the samples tested at 800 °C and 900 °C, an almost fully oxide-covered surface can be observed, which is relatively smooth and exhibits some grooves.
Furthermore, the appearance indicates abrasive wear of the oxides.
